items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-29
items.q: I've never heard of Cuban Bennett.

ctx.x: Well, Alvin told me that he liked Cuban Bennett a lot.

That's the fellow I'm referring to, but I've never heard of Cuban Bennett. But they claim he had this type of trumpet that he played. Well, if Billy Douglas copied it, he did an awful, tremendous job of copying so much.
One more, maybe. See what's next. We'll have time for one more.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Did you ever hear him talk about Cuba? Cuban Bennett?

ctx.x: Well, when the band first left here, when I organized it here in New Orleans, there weren't any arrangers. We would take the stocks and we would rearrange the stocks to fit what we wanted, and how we wanted it. But we were concentrating on our original style of playing. And the first arranger that I had in the band was a fellow out of Little Rock, Arkansas. He is still living today. His name is Philander Tiller, an alto player. Now, Phil was a tremendous arranger. And he could write arrangements that he couldn't…
Did you ever hear him talk about Cuba? Cuban Bennett?
No, Bennett Douglas was a strange fellow. He never talked about anything in common. I remember you asking me about that, but no, he never mentioned anyone.
